title: Arc-disjoint directed paths from an excess to a deficit vertex
statement:
Let $D$ be a finite digraph, let $x 
eq y$ be two of its vertices, and let $l$ be a natural number. Suppose that $d^{+}(x) - d^{-}(x) = l$ and $d^{-}(y) - d^{+}(y) = l$, and that every other vertex $v$ (that is, $v 
eq x$ and $v 
eq y$) satisfies $d^{+}(v) = d^{-}(v)$, where $d^{+}$ and $d^{-}$ denote outdegree and indegree. Then $D$ contains $l$ pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths from $x$ to $y$.
replaced:
\emph{Let \texttt{D} be a digraph such that (i)
\texttt{d$^{+}$(x) - d$^{-}$(x) = l = d$^{-}$(y) - d$^{+}$(y)} and (ii) \texttt{d$^{+}$(v) = d$^{-}$(v)} for
\texttt{v $\in$ V \textbackslash{} \{x, y\}}.  Show, using exercise 10.3.2, that there exist \texttt{l} arc-disjoint
directed \texttt{(x, y)}-paths in \texttt{D}.}
